turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so tell me who made that decision and when.
"Get this over with." That's how this whole thing was handled, Hale, and I'm writing that down. I asked who decided on the zero, and when.
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My son does not lie, and you just called him a cheater to his mother's face with nothing in your hand. "Everyone knows it" is gossip, Hale, not evidence. Show me a document, or I walk down to the principal's office right now.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
I haven't raised my voice once, Hale. I've asked one question three times: who decided on the zero, and on what basis? Answer it, or I'm going upstairs.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

"Wasting my time." You asked for this meeting, Hale, and you have nothing to put on the table. When I leave this room I'm going straight to the principal, and the first thing I'll ask for is how this zero got entered under your own school's procedure 4.2.
